name: The Beatles
bio_short: The most influential band of the 1960s, formed in Liverpool by John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr. Their evolution from beat-pop to studio experimentation reshaped popular music.

name: The Rolling Stones
bio_short: Blues-rooted London band led by Mick Jagger and Keith Richards that became the defining 'bad boy' counterpart to The Beatles during the British Invasion.

name: The Who
bio_short: Explosive mod-era band known for Pete Townshend's power chords, Keith Moon's drumming and rock-opera ambitions like 'Tommy'.

name: The Kinks
bio_short: Ray Davies-led band whose distorted riff on 'You Really Got Me' helped invent hard rock, later pivoting to wry, distinctly English songwriting.

name: The Animals
bio_short: Gritty R&B-driven group fronted by Eric Burdon, best known for the transatlantic No. 1 'House of the Rising Sun'.

name: The Dave Clark Five
bio_short: Drummer-led beat group whose stomping 'Tottenham Sound' briefly rivaled The Beatles and made a record number of Ed Sullivan Show appearances.

name: Herman's Hermits
bio_short: Clean-cut Manchester pop group fronted by Peter Noone that scored a run of cheerful transatlantic hits in the mid-1960s.

name: The Yardbirds
bio_short: Blues-rock incubator famous for launching guitarists Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck and Jimmy Page and for pioneering the 'rave-up'.

name: The Searchers
bio_short: Liverpool Merseybeat band known for jangling twelve-string guitar and tight harmonies on hits like 'Needles and Pins'.

name: The Doors
bio_short: L.A. quartet built around Jim Morrison's poetry and Ray Manzarek's organ, blending blues, jazz and dark theatricality.

name: Jefferson Airplane
bio_short: Leading San Francisco psychedelic band, powered by Grace Slick's vocals on 'White Rabbit' and 'Somebody to Love'.

name: The Jimi Hendrix Experience
bio_short: Power trio that showcased Jimi Hendrix's revolutionary electric-guitar technique and feedback-drenched psychedelia.

name: Pink Floyd
bio_short: British band whose early Syd Barrett era defined UK psychedelia before evolving into progressive rock pioneers.

name: The Byrds
bio_short: Roger McGuinn's twelve-string Rickenbacker gave the band its chiming signature, bridging folk-rock and early psychedelia.

name: The Grateful Dead
bio_short: Improvisation-driven San Francisco band that grew from the acid-test scene into a touring institution led by Jerry Garcia.

name: Country Joe and the Fish
bio_short: Berkeley band that fused psychedelia with pointed anti-Vietnam War satire, epitomized by the 'I-Feel-Like-I'm-Fixin'-to-Die Rag'.

name: The 13th Floor Elevators
bio_short: Texas group often credited with coining the term 'psychedelic rock,' distinguished by Roky Erickson's wail and the electric jug.

name: Love
bio_short: Arthur Lee's racially integrated L.A. band whose 1967 album 'Forever Changes' is a landmark of baroque psychedelia.

name: The Beach Boys
bio_short: Brian Wilson's California group defined surf-pop harmony before expanding into the ambitious studio craft of 'Pet Sounds'.

name: The Ventures
bio_short: Hugely influential instrumental group whose clean guitar sound on 'Walk, Don't Run' inspired countless bands worldwide.

name: The Standells
bio_short: L.A. garage band whose snarling 'Dirty Water' became an enduring anthem, later adopted by Boston sports fans.

name: The Sonics
bio_short: Raw, distorted Pacific Northwest band widely cited as a proto-punk influence for its ferocious early recordings.

name: Dick Dale
bio_short: The 'King of the Surf Guitar,' whose staccato, reverb-heavy Middle-Eastern-tinged playing defined instrumental surf rock.

name: The Kingsmen
bio_short: Portland group whose famously murky recording of 'Louie Louie' became one of rock's most iconic garage records.

name: Sam the Sham and the Pharaohs
bio_short: Tex-Mex flavored novelty-rock band, costumed in turbans, best known for the raucous 'Wooly Bully'.

name: The Seeds
bio_short: Sky Saxon's L.A. band whose primitive, organ-driven 'Pushin' Too Hard' epitomized the garage-punk template.

name: Count Five
bio_short: San Jose teenagers whose fuzz-guitar hit 'Psychotic Reaction' became a garage-rock classic.

name: Bob Dylan
bio_short: The era's defining songwriter, who moved from acoustic protest folk to electric rock in 1965 and won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Simon & Garfunkel
bio_short: Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel's harmony duo whose literate songs like 'The Sound of Silence' defined introspective folk-rock.

name: Joan Baez
bio_short: Soprano-voiced folk icon and civil-rights activist who helped popularize Bob Dylan's early songs.

name: Peter, Paul and Mary
bio_short: Popular folk trio central to the 1960s protest movement, scoring hits with 'If I Had a Hammer' and Dylan covers.

name: Donovan
bio_short: Scottish singer-songwriter who blended folk with psychedelia and jazz on hits like 'Sunshine Superman' and 'Season of the Witch'.

name: The Mamas & The Papas
bio_short: Lush harmony group led by John Phillips whose 'California Dreamin'' captured the mid-decade folk-rock sound.

name: Leonard Cohen
bio_short: Canadian poet and novelist who turned to songwriting in 1967, bringing literary depth to folk with 'Suzanne' and 'So Long, Marianne'.

name: Scott McKenzie
bio_short: American singer whose 1967 anthem 'San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Flowers in Your Hair)' became the Summer of Love's signature song.

name: The Supremes
bio_short: Motown's most successful act and the most charting American vocal group, led for its peak by Diana Ross.

name: The Four Tops
bio_short: Long-running Motown vocal quartet, with Levi Stubbs's urgent lead voice powering 'Reach Out I'll Be There'.

name: The Temptations
bio_short: Signature Motown group known for sharp choreography and layered harmonies on 'My Girl' and 'Get Ready'.

name: Marvin Gaye
bio_short: Versatile Motown star whose smooth voice and later socially conscious work made him one of soul's defining artists.

name: Smokey Robinson & The Miracles
bio_short: Group led by Smokey Robinson, one of Motown's principal songwriters, celebrated for melodic, poetic soul.

name: Martha and the Vandellas
bio_short: Powerhouse Motown trio whose 'Dancing in the Street' and 'Heat Wave' brought raw energy to the label's sound.

name: Stevie Wonder
bio_short: Child prodigy signed to Motown at 11 who became a multi-instrumentalist innovator and one of the most awarded artists ever.

name: Aretha Franklin
bio_short: The 'Queen of Soul,' whose gospel-rooted voice and 1967 recording of 'Respect' made her a cultural landmark.

name: James Brown
bio_short: The 'Godfather of Soul,' whose rhythmic innovations laid the groundwork for funk and, later, hip-hop.

name: Johnny Cash
bio_short: The 'Man in Black,' whose deep voice and outlaw image bridged country, rockabilly and folk audiences.

name: Patsy Cline
bio_short: Pioneering vocalist of the Nashville Sound whose emotive delivery on 'Crazy' crossed country into pop before her death at 30.

name: Buck Owens
bio_short: Architect of the twangy, electric 'Bakersfield Sound' that offered a rougher alternative to polished Nashville country.

name: Merle Haggard
bio_short: Bakersfield giant and ex-convict whose autobiographical songs like 'Mama Tried' made him a country institution.

name: Tammy Wynette
bio_short: The 'First Lady of Country Music,' whose 'Stand By Your Man' became one of the genre's best-selling singles.

name: Glen Campbell
bio_short: Crossover star and ace session guitarist whose Jimmy Webb collaborations produced 'Wichita Lineman' and 'By the Time I Get to Phoenix'.

name: Roger Miller
bio_short: Witty singer-songwriter whose playful hits 'King of the Road' and 'Dang Me' won a then-record haul of Grammys.

name: Loretta Lynn
bio_short: Coal-miner's daughter whose candid, woman's-perspective songwriting broke new ground in country music.

name: The Monkees
bio_short: Made-for-TV pop group whose catchy, Brill-Building-supplied hits and hit series became a mid-60s phenomenon.

name: The Four Seasons
bio_short: Frankie Valli's falsetto-led group that strung together doo-wop-infused pop chart-toppers like 'Sherry' and 'Walk Like a Man'.

name: The Ronettes
bio_short: Girl group fronted by Ronnie Spector whose 'Be My Baby' epitomized Phil Spector's 'Wall of Sound'.

name: Lesley Gore
bio_short: Teen-pop star whose 'It's My Party' and the proto-feminist 'You Don't Own Me' made her a defining early-60s voice.

name: The Shangri-Las
bio_short: Girl group known for melodramatic 'death-disc' teen sagas, most famously 'Leader of the Pack'.

name: The Turtles
bio_short: L.A. pop-rock band that topped the charts with the sunny 'Happy Together' in 1967.

name: The Shirelles
bio_short: One of the first successful girl groups; their 'Will You Love Me Tomorrow' was the first US No. 1 by a Black girl group.

name: The Crystals
bio_short: Phil Spector-produced girl group behind Wall-of-Sound hits 'Da Doo Ron Ron' and 'Then He Kissed Me'.

name: The Young Rascals
bio_short: Blue-eyed soul group whose energetic 'Good Lovin'' and mellow 'Groovin'' were mid-60s staples.

name: Frank Sinatra
bio_short: The premier American pop-jazz vocalist, whose phrasing and 1960s Reprise recordings defined adult popular song.

name: Tony Bennett
bio_short: Enduring interpreter of the Great American Songbook, signature song 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco'.

name: Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass
bio_short: Trumpeter-led instrumental group whose bright 'Ameriachi' sound dominated mid-60s easy-listening charts.

name: Dionne Warwick
bio_short: Sophisticated pop-soul singer whose long partnership with Burt Bacharach and Hal David produced a string of elegant hits.

name: Henry Mancini
bio_short: Prolific film and TV composer of 'Moon River' and the 'Pink Panther' theme, a giant of orchestral easy listening.

name: Stan Getz
bio_short: Lyrical tenor saxophonist whose bossa nova recordings, notably 'The Girl from Ipanema,' sparked a US Latin-jazz craze.

name: Wes Montgomery
bio_short: Innovative jazz guitarist famed for his thumb-picked octave style, later crossing into pop-jazz success.

name: Astrud Gilberto
bio_short: Brazilian singer whose understated English vocal on 'The Girl from Ipanema' became the face of the bossa nova wave.

name: Burt Bacharach
bio_short: Influential composer-arranger whose sophisticated melodies and unusual time signatures defined 1960s sophisticated pop.
